slides.title: Five brand attributes
bullets: **Native —** finishes a status code HTTP already reserved; ask "does HTTP already say this" first. (the-standard)
**Instant —** settles in about two seconds; no loading states or multi-step narratives in copy. (agentic-commerce)
**Machine-first —** most traffic is read by an agent; unambiguous beats persuasive. (agentic-commerce)
**Open —** a protocol, not a product; no license to implement, no single gatekeeper. (open-neutral)
**Unadorned —** a black-and-white wordmark; no gradient, mascot or color story. (brand page)
slides.source: From x402.org/brand-guidelines (read 8 Oct 2026), each mapped to the Messaging Document pillar it expresses. The test every later design and copy decision is checked against.

slides.title: The wordmark on a plain field is the primary lockup. The x402 Foundation has its own.
slides.notes: Files: x402 logos — https://x402.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/10/2026/09/x402_logo.zip; x402 Foundation logos — https://x402.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/10/2026/09/x402_foundation-logo.zip. The wordmark is a custom-cut mark, never reproduced in a font. Owner: x402 Foundation marketing; final art by LF Creative Services.

slides.title: One mark, four surfaces
slides.source: Black on White and on light surfaces; white on Ink and on the site's green. The logo appears only in pure black or pure white.

slides.title: Minimum size: 32 px, then the symbol
slides.source: The lockup holds to 32 px tall; below that the crossbar strokes fight at screen resolution, so use the symbol alone, legible to about 14 px. Documented.

slides.title: Clear space is measured in X
slides.source: X = one quarter of the x-mark's height, so it scales with the logo. At least X of empty space on all four sides, for the lockup and for the symbol alone. Documented.

slides.title: Partnership lockups
slides.source: Beside a facilitator, implementer or partner mark: a vertical divider 1.5× the lockup's height; size the partner mark to equal visual weight, not equal width. Documented.

slides.title: Watchouts
slides.source: The six ways the mark gets damaged. Any of them breaks the Unadorned attribute the system is built on. Also never imply affiliation or endorsement.
slides.notes: Stretching or distorting; recoloring away from pure black or white; rotating off the baseline; busy or low-contrast backgrounds; drop shadows or glows; separating or rearranging the wordmark's elements.

slides.title: The symbol on its own
slides.source: The crossing strokes of the x read alone: favicons, tabs, app icons, avatars, package-registry profiles, watermarks. Two colorways, black and white; in a circle or rounded square with one X of margin.
slides.notes: The symbol file in this example is a crop of the wordmark for testing the renderer; the production symbol is in the brand page's logo zip.

slides.title: Primary and secondary palette
slides.source: Primary: Ink and Paper — pure black and white from the logo files; the contrast between them does what a brand color normally does. Secondary: four grey tints for body copy, secondary text, hairlines and surfaces. Documented.

slides.title: We are / we are not

rows: Neutral, permissionless, inviting. Anyone can build on or extend x402 without asking; members' products are peers.
Chaotic. Open means neutral governance and open process, not an absence of review.
Authoritative the way a specification is: exact terms, present tense, every figure with its window, source and date.
Exclusionary. Definitive means authoritative, not 'the only'; no superlative without its proof point.
Trust-minimizing and precise: name the mechanism, state the boundary.
Claiming risk-free. 'Unhackable', 'bulletproof', '100% secure' are never used.

slides.source: Sounds like: "The facilitator settles the payment. It can only move what you signed for." · Doesn't sound like: "The most secure payment rail ever built." Derived from the Messaging Document pillars and the ED's adjectives.

slides.title: Prefer this, avoid that

rows: Brand casing; the mark is held by LF Projects, LLC
Every figure carries its window and date
A peer standard from a Premier member exists
'formal liaison with the Agentic AI Foundation'
Protocol terms defined on first use; no chain jargon
Exclamation points, memes, slang in owned channels
Instant: nothing takes longer to read than the payment takes to clear

slides.source: Reading level: 8th grade for web, social and executive content; developer content may go denser. Confident about the protocol, humble about the roadmap. Contractions in web and social, none in specs and press releases.

slides.title: Using the brand: what third parties may do
bullets: **In general —** nothing that confuses, misleads or implies sponsorship; your mark more prominent than ours; never edit the logo.
**Advertising and sales —** check with us first; "x402 Member" in text is fine when true.
**Education —** no logos on book covers; add "[Title] is not affiliated with or otherwise sponsored by x402."
**Names and domains —** no x402 in a company, product or domain name; no folding our logo into yours.
**Merchandise —** not by third parties without permission.
slides.notes: Full text: x402.org/brand-guidelines#legal, under the LF Projects, LLC Terms of Use and Trademark Policy. Questions: the brand page's contact address; send a mockup; allow two weeks; no response does not mean approval. Co-branding on LF templates: the x402 wordmark replaces the LF logo; the LF lockup on the closing slide or in the boilerplate; member logos only with permission and never beside a comparison. Final visual sign-off: LF Creative Services, brand@linuxfoundation.org.
